# Brush Stroke

**Cover › Stroke** · v1.0.0 · 60 frames at 30 fps (30–100)

A thick, rough brush paints across the frame in a few passes until it is covered, then the stroke wipes away to show the next scene.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/brush-stroke@1.0.0.mp4) · [Alpha overlay for editing apps](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/brush-stroke@1.0.0-overlay.mov)

## Where it is used

- Handmade and artistic edits
- Travel and lifestyle
- Titles over paint

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import brushStroke from './transitions/04-cover/stroke/brush-stroke';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(brushStroke, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 60 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `color` | color | `"#FF4F1A"` |  | The incoming scene's background colour; the transition brings it in. |
| `passes` | integer | `4` | 2–7 | How many back-and-forth strokes cover the frame. |
| `seed` | integer | `1` | 0–9999 | Changes the random layout. |
| `hold` | number | `0.1` | 0–0.4 | Share of the transition spent fully covered. |
